content.text:
I submitted **index 0 (Sb fraction 0.134)** as the best composition. At 0.227%, it had the highest EQE of the five I measured.

I used all 5 EQE measurements and none of the 5 XRD measurements. So I never checked which crystal phases are actually present in the films.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.134 | **0.227** |
| 5 | 0.210 | 0.184 |
| 9 | 0.303 | 0.154 |
| 15 | 0.493 | 0.083 |
| 19 | 0.629 | 0.079 |

- **How I picked the first three:** I measured the three compositions sitting at known In–Sb–O compounds: In11Sb3O24 (index 5), InSbO4 (index 15) and In3Sb5O12 (index 19). The predicted band gaps are 1.9, 2.2 and 2.8 eV, all below the 3.2 eV light, so each could absorb it.
- **Trend:** EQE went up every time the Sb fraction went down. Index 0 is the lowest-Sb composition on the line, so the true peak may lie at even lower Sb, beyond what this line covers.
- **Untested gaps:** The GP model also suggested indices 8, 10 and 11, and it predicted that 8 could come close to index 0. Most compositions between indices 0 and 9 were never measured, so one of them could beat index 0.
